learning_outcomes.title: Tests for parallelograms
learning_outcomes.statement: Recognize the conditions that ensure a quadrilateral is a parallelogram.
learning_outcomes.rule_summary: Sufficient tests include both pairs of opposite sides congruent, both pairs of opposite angles congruent, diagonals bisecting each other, or one pair of opposite sides both parallel and congruent.

questions.instruction: Determine whether the markings guarantee a parallelogram. Choose the correct justification.
questions.stem: Determine whether the markings guarantee a parallelogram. Choose the correct justification.

options.text: Yes: one pair of opposite sides is both parallel and congruent.
Yes: the diagonals are marked perpendicular.
No: a parallelogram cannot have these markings.
Yes: any one pair of congruent sides is sufficient.

answer.correct_option_text: Yes: one pair of opposite sides is both parallel and congruent.
answer.explanation: A single pair that is BOTH parallel and congruent is sufficient.

answer.explanation: These conditions also describe an isosceles trapezoid; the same pair would need to be both parallel and congruent.
